component.name: Voice Changer
component.summary: Realtime voice changer that shows up as a microphone

description.p: Voice Changer processes your microphone in real time and publishes the result as a new PipeWire microphone called "Voice Changer Mic", so Discord, SIP clients, OBS and anything else can simply select it. The same engine also loads as a CLAP plugin in DAWs.

ul.li: Natural pitch and formant shifting (pitch-synchronous, the technique hardware voice transformers use) plus phase-vocoder modes
Drive, robot, echo, reverb and tone effects with ready-made voices: Man, Woman, Baritone, Bass, Deep, Demon, Monster, Chipmunk, Robot, Radio, Cave, Announcer
Local AI voice conversion with RVC v2 models, including retrieval indices, on the CPU or an AMD GPU
Neural noise suppression and a voice-only gate before everything else
One big on/off switch: window, tray icon, global shortcut or the command line
Hear-myself monitoring, presets, favourites, and a voice library that imports from a pasted link

screenshot.caption: Home: presets, quick tweaks and the AI voice card
Voices: import and manage AI voice models
Effects: pitch engine and effect panels
Settings: microphone, window behaviour, hotkey and logs

description.p: A reworked interface: level meters with a scale and a clip warning, a Mute button and shortcut, an output picker, presets you can rename, update, share and import, first steps that tick themselves off, plain-language labels, and problems explained next to the button that fixes them. The delay shown now includes the AI voice. Scrolling a page no longer changes controls. NVIDIA set-up needs only the driver. There is also a first Windows version.

The AI voice answers about twice as fast (around half a second on a GPU). Coughs, burps and sneezes are silenced instead of converted; quiet breaths stay quiet; each voice remembers its own pitch and index settings. A test bench replays a recording of you through any voice while you tune it, and new voices are checked for problems at import. Voice pages from voice-models.com can be pasted directly. Hear myself no longer makes other sound stutter.

AI voices no longer crash the app on machines that use the CPU engine (every NVIDIA and Intel machine by default). NVIDIA set-up is one command, and the app says plainly when a GPU cannot be used. The microphone, the virtual microphone and Hear myself now run on one clock; quitting always gives the system its default microphone back.
Fixes a crash at start on machines that have the ROCm ONNX Runtime installed but no AMD GPU: the CPU runtime is used there instead.

Runs on many more Linux computers: portable builds for glibc 2.35 and newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Mint 21, Zorin 17), an aarch64 build, a Flatpak bundle and an AUR recipe. The AI picks its thread count from your processor, with an override in Settings. Audio problems are explained in the window with a Retry button, PipeWire restarts are survived, an unplugged microphone falls back and comes back, and a "voice-changer doctor" command checks the machine. A welcome card guides the first start and the window shows how many apps are hearing the voice.
Fixes the AI voice muting your microphone while it warms up or drops a block, keeps the voice effects working during warm-up, and makes "Replace my microphone everywhere" move every recording app.
The virtual microphone now works with PulseAudio apps (Discord, browsers, OBS); it is a proper driver node instead of a pw_stream source.
Fixes "use as the microphone for everything" silencing apps (a capture feedback loop) and "hear myself" producing no sound.
Keeps the virtual microphone at full volume and names Electron apps by their process in the routing list.
Fixes voice import on fresh machines (missing scipy in the converter environment).
NVIDIA GPU support through ONNX Runtime's CUDA provider; the gpu feature now covers ROCm and CUDA.
First release: natural pitch engine, effects, presets, AI voices with retrieval index, GPU support, iced interface, tray, hotkey, D-Bus and CLI.
